This site is more than rendered pages: the Guided Research Assistant is
backed by a function-calling agent, a quantitative evaluation harness, and
a public MCP research-data service. This page documents that engineering
work — the architecture, the design decisions, and the measured results.

## System architecture: layered contracts

The core design principle is a **layered contract** (ADR-0010, ADR-0014):
task selection is always an explicit visitor action — no LLM ever guesses
which task was intended — while *within* the selected task boundary, a
bounded agent autonomously orchestrates typed tools over **Study
Evidence**: the published ALIGATEHR-Gen paper plus the published study
result data.

```{mermaid}
flowchart TB
    subgraph UX["Task routing layer — explicit, no intent classification"]
        MENU["Research Task Menu"]
        PQ["Understand the Research"]
        VIZ["Explore Visualizations"]
        WIZ["Build a Demo Profile"]
    end
    subgraph AGENT["In-task agent — bounded tool orchestration"]
        LOOP["Function-calling loop<br/>max 6 iterations, final turn must be text"]
    end
    subgraph TOOLS["Typed Study Evidence tools (Pydantic-validated)"]
        T1["get_paper_content"]
        T2["query_metrics"]
        T3["query_ablation"]
        T4["query_enrichment"]
        T5["summarize_fibrotic_cohort<br/>aggregates only"]
    end
    subgraph GOV["Data governance boundary"]
        PUB["Display-safe release<br/>(public)"]
        PRIV["Private matching artifact<br/>(never exposed;<br/>suppression-minimum aggregates only)"]
    end
    MENU --> PQ & VIZ & WIZ
    PQ --> LOOP
    VIZ -->|direct navigation| GOV
    WIZ -->|structured /profile endpoints| PRIV
    LOOP --> T1 & T2 & T3 & T4 & T5
    T5 --> PRIV
    T2 & T3 & T4 --> PUB
    MCP["MCP clients<br/>(Claude Desktop, Cursor, ...)"] -->|/mcp Streamable HTTP| TOOLS
```

The agent loop is deliberately **framework-free** — roughly a hundred
lines against DeepSeek's OpenAI-compatible function-calling API. Owning
the loop keeps the product's core mechanism fully inspectable, and the
provider remains a config-level swap. Malformed or unknown tool calls are
returned to the model as explicit error payloads in a normal tool turn —
general protocol handling, never a silent retry.

Guardrails are **specified outputs, not keyword filters**: the system
prompt defines a scope contract (research explanation and cohort-level
statistics only; personal risk questions are refused and redirected to the
structured Demo Profile task; questions outside Study Evidence receive an
explicit scope limitation), and that behavior is *verified by adversarial
evaluation items* rather than input filtering.

## Evaluation: three generations, one golden set

Every architecture generation was measured on the same 36-item golden set
(single-tool, multi-tool compositional, adversarial, ambiguous — including
questions about the in-progress Bio-E2R manuscript, which is deliberately
*outside* the answering scope until published). The single-call baseline
was captured **before** the agent cutover replaced it, and is preserved
under the `paper-question-single-call` git tag.

| Path | Overall | Single-tool | Multi-tool | Adversarial refusal | Mean LLM calls | Mean latency |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Legacy intent router | 41.7% | 38.5% | 27.3% | 85.7% | 1.75 | 3.3s |
| Single-call full-paper injection | 27.8% | 30.8% | **0.0%** | 71.4% | 1.0 | 2.3s |
| **In-task agent (live)** | **94.4%** | **100%** | **100%** | **100%** | 2.22 | 6.4s |

The headline: multi-tool compositional questions — "which ablation hurt
CKD most, and does that align with the paper's claims?" — went from
**structurally unanswerable (0%)** to **100%**. Tool selection is measured
judge-free from recorded call traces: 91.7% exact match, 100% coverage.

Methodology, honestly stated: correctness is graded by an LLM judge
(DeepSeek, temperature 0, written rubric with per-item grading notes),
which shares a model family with the system under test. Mitigations: 22%
of agent verdicts were manually re-checked (zero disagreements), the
tool-trace metric requires no judge at all, and all raw and graded results
are committed in the repository (`chatbot-backend/eval/results/`). The
residual weakness is also reported: on deliberately ambiguous questions
the agent clarifies only 40% of the time, preferring answers with
explicitly labeled assumptions.

The latency cost of orchestration (2.3s → 6.4s mean) is a deliberate
trade: correctness dominates in research Q&A, and the streaming endpoint
(below) makes the work visible while it happens.

## Streaming agent UX

Answers stream over Server-Sent Events (`POST /paper/question/stream`)
with four event types — `tool_call`, `tool_result`, `token`, `done` — so
the widget shows *what the agent is consulting* ("Consulting ablation
results… ✓") before the answer streams in token by token. The widget
falls back to the non-streaming endpoint only on connection failure;
mid-stream errors are terminal and never silently refetched. The frontend
stays vanilla JS: the SSE client is a small, unit-tested UMD module.

## MCP: the tools as a public research-data service

The same tool registry is exposed over the Model Context Protocol
(ADR-0015), so any MCP client can query the study directly. The transport
is Streamable HTTP mounted at `/mcp` on the same FastAPI service — one
container, one port — stateless with JSON responses. The MCP roster is a
strict superset of the agent's: seven read-only tools, adding validated
ICD keyword lookup and the raw display-safe embedding release. Every call
routes through the same Pydantic validation layer the agent uses, so the
two surfaces cannot drift.

Connect from Claude Desktop (Settings → Connectors → Add custom
connector):

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "aligatehr-research": {
      "type": "http",
      "url": "https://aligatehr-gen-backend.onrender.com/mcp/"
    }
  }
}
```

The governance boundary is absolute: the Demo Profile flow, the private
matching artifact, and anything patient-level are not on this surface.
Cohort statistics appear only as aggregates that respect the release's
cell-suppression minimum — the same privacy class as the site's Matched
Reference Summary.

## Decision records

The non-obvious choices are written down as ADRs in
[`docs/adr/`](https://github.com/PatrickTangwen/report-web/tree/main/docs/adr):
grounding Paper Question Mode in Study Evidence (0013, partially
superseding the paper-only contract), in-task agent orchestration instead
of intent routing (0014), and the MCP exposure with its governance
boundary (0015) — on top of the earlier Guided Research Assistant
redesign records (0008–0012).
